pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: drm/rockchip: dw-mipi-dsi: don't configure hardware in mode_set for MIPI With atomic modesetting the hardware will be powered off when the mode_set function is called. We should configure the hardware in the enable function, which is the atomic version of "commit" so let's use the enable hook rather than commit while we're at it. UPSTREAM: drm/rockchip: dw-mipi-dsi: properly configure PHY timing These values are specified as constant time periods but the PHY configuration is in terms of the current lane byte clock so using constant values guarantees that the timings will be outside the specification with some display configurations. Derive the necessary configuration from the byte clock in order to ensure that the PHY configuration is correct. BUG=chrome-os-partner:62134 TEST=check mipi screen, it can display normally Signed-off-by: John Keeping <john@metanate.com> Signed-off-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20170224125506.21533-17-john@metanate.com (cherry picked from git://anongit.freedesktop.org/drm-misc drm-misc-next commit 3fdfb4f170df4d113a3b6663ebf115e10601d0e9) Change-Id:I0e6ddd6395a65eb9a1723639339af5ec7c9d1976 Signed-off-by: Chris Zhong <zyw@rock-chips.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/431273 Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm/rockchip: dw-mipi-dsi: improve PLL configuration The multiplication ratio for the PLL is required to be even due to the use of a "by 2 pre-scaler". Currently we are likely to end up with an odd multiplier even though there is an equivalent set of parameters with an even multiplier. For example, using the 324MHz bit rate with a reference clock of 24MHz we end up with M = 27, N = 2 whereas the example in the PHY databook gives M = 54, N = 4 for this bit rate and reference clock. By walking down through the available multiplier instead of up we are more likely to hit an even multiplier. With the above example we do now get M = 54, N = 4 as given by the databook. While doing this, change the loop limits to encode the actual limits on the divisor, which are: 40MHz >= (pllref / N) >= 5MHz BUG=chrome-os-partner:62134 TEST=check mipi screen, it can display normally Signed-off-by: John Keeping <john@metanate.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20170224125506.21533-18-john@metanate.com (cherry picked from git://anongit.freedesktop.org/drm-misc drm-misc-next commit b0a45fec5974f84aff7c249f7da6674f81b61bf6) Change-Id:I5f3292797ee563e8455d4baaffc7d116283a4336 Signed-off-by: Chris Zhong <zyw@rock-chips.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/431274 Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ASoC: rt5514: Make hotword implementation compatible with Chrome Without this patch, the current hotword implementation works like this: 1. Userspace ensures no DMIC capture is active. 2. Userspace set kcontrol "DSP Voice Wake Up" to ON to load DSP fw and arm the DSP for hotword detection. The codec has to be in SND_SOC_BIAS_OFF, otherwise the kcontrol put is a no-op. 3. If a normal capture stream is started at this point, DSP is automatically turned off by codec driver, no auto re-arm. 4. DSP detects a hotword (IRQ is not wired up yet) 5. Userspace opens the hotword PCM device to read after a hotword is detected (needs IRQ notification). 6. Codec driver only sends 2sec of audio to the PCM device, then stops. 7. Userspace closes the hotword PCM device. This patch removes the kcontrol. Hotword detection starts when userspace opens the hotword PCM device. IRQ is wired up so that the hotword PCM device starts streaming when a hotword is detected. Normal capture and hotwording usecases are coordinated by the codec driver with mutex and a state machine. Normal capture has higher priority. Starting a normal capture while DSP is armed or streaming, pauses the DSP. When the normal capture stream is closed, DSP is auto re-armed. The hotword PCM device streams 2sec of audio first, following by zeros until it's closed. The new hotword implementation works like this: 1. Userspace can open/close the hotword PCM device anytime to indicate it wants hotword detection to start/stop. 2. Userspace can start normal capture anytime, though hotword will not be detected when normal capture is active. 3. Hotword detection is notified to userspace by the availability of samples from the hotword PCM device. BUG=b:35572001 TEST=sequences of normal capture and hotword detection Change-Id: I8bb5f5b4efb7324239ac72b25a2e7e640c8105ba Signed-off-by: Ben Zhang <benzh@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/444275 Commit-Ready: Chinyue Chen <chinyue@chromium.org> Tested-by: Chinyue Chen <chinyue@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: iwl7000: chromeOS: fix Intel regulatory (de)registration This is a re-land of commit b4803ed63478, with the erroneous KERNEL_VERSION ifdefs removed. --- Since callers can assume, due to the way this works in the normal cfg80211, that the wiphy pointer is valid even when the device has been or is being unregistered, defer the intel regulatory deregistration until free. To make error cases work correctly, also do the registration at alloc. Also squashed with: "CHROMIUM: iwl7000: chromeOS: register Intel regulatory in register_hw() This partially reverts my previous change: moving the regulatory registration into alloc_hw() is broken since then by that point the REGULATORY_WIPHY_SELF_MANAGED flag can't have been set yet, and thus registration will be ignored. I originally moved the register to be symmetric with unregister (which moved to free), but since unregister is idempotent and doesn't care if you unregister something that was never actually registered, it's safe to register only in register_hw() and yet unregister in free_hw()." goofy: set default options by py/goofy/goofy.json If we want to pass additional options when starting goofy, we need to find a way to modify GOOFY_ARGS in sh/goofy_control.sh. And this usually includes adding complicated logic in board_setup_factory.sh. However, if this goofy option is required for a not-board-specific application, such as running goofy on whale fixture, then we should not put this logic into board_setup_factory.sh. Since we don't want user to copy and paste this logic from old project to new project. This CL allows you to add default options to goofy by editing py/goofy/goofy.json. For example, if you want to restart test list everytime, you can set goofy.json to: { "restart": true } By makding this a part of setup steps of Whale fixture, or make the toolkit for Whale fixture include this goofy.json by default, Whale fixture setup and startup process doesn't need to be part of board_setup_factory anymore. We can create an init/main.d/whale_host.sh in factory repo, and future projects can reuse it directly.
